title: Argentina’s Joaquin Panichelli, Ligue 1 top scorer, suffers ACL tear in right knee
content:
Strasbourg forward Joaquin Panichelli has sustained an anterior cruciate ligament tear in his right knee while on international duty with Argentina.

The Argentine Football Association confirmed the news on Friday, having previously said that the 23-year-old would undergo tests after suffering the injury during training a day earlier.

Panichelli is the top scorer in Ligue 1 this season with 16 goals in 27 matches. He was featuring in only his second national team camp with Argentina, having made his first appearance for his country in a November friendly against Angola.

The injury rules Panichelli out of contention for the rest of the season so he will miss the World Cup this summer, with ACL tears taking around nine months to recover from.

Panichelli only joined Strasbourg last July, having scored 20 goals in 40 Spanish second-tier matches for Cordoba in 2024-25, on loan from La Liga side Alaves.

In this Argentina camp, Panichelli was part of a group of forwards including Lionel Messi, Julian Alvarez and Jose Manuel Lopez. Lionel Scaloni’s side face Mauritania and Zambia in home friendlies after the Finalissima against Spain was cancelled due to the conflict in the Middle East.

Analysis by Tom Burrows

For Strasbourg, news of star striker Joaquin Panichelli’s ACL injury is their worst nightmare.

Since joining in the summer from Deportivo Alavés, Panichelli has been in fantastic form, scoring 20 goals in all competitions. He is the top goalscorer in Ligue 1 and has seven goals in his last eight appearances for Gary O’Neil’s side.

His goals have been a mix of instinctive strikers’ finishes, headers, tap-ins, while he is also Strasbourg’s penalty taker.

The 23-year-old has stepped up in the absence of fellow striker Emmanuel Emegha, who has been injured for much of the campaign. It was announced in September that captain Emegha will join Chelsea this summer, which caused controversy among Strasbourg’s fanbase.

In a previous interview with The Athletic, Liam Rosenior, his former head coach at Strasbourg, described Panichelli as a “throwback.” “He’s an old school centre forward, he’s like an Argentinian Alan Shearer. You don’t get many of those types of strikers any more,” he said.

Meanwhile, in an interview with UEFA, Panichelli said he modelled his game on French striker Olivier Giroud.

“I saw myself in him,” he said. “He wasn’t just a goalscorer. When he dropped deep, he helped the team in the build-up play. He’s always been one of my main role models, just like Karim Benzema or, today, Harry Kane.”

Panichelli’s performances have put him on the radar of clubs across Europe and he made his debut for Argentina in November.

His injury comes at a terrible time for Strasbourg, who are eighth in Ligue 1 and fighting for a European spot.

They are also in the quarter-final of the Conference League, where they face German side Mainz, and have reached the semi-final of the Coupe de France, where they play at home to struggling Nice on April 22.

As reported by Reuters, Panichelli previously suffered a cruciate ligament tear in July 2023, which meant he missed six months of football.
